coverage: Native Enter Amount buttons construct actual Paper dialogs with one bounded text input, current value, Use amount and Cancel actions.
0.50 unit price saves exactly fifty cents only in setup draft; separate review and final publication remain unchanged.
19 bread bundles review as 304 items and $760.00 without debit or delivery; final purchase confirmation remains separate.
Zero, fractional and out-of-stock quantities and excessive price precision reopen a fresh input dialog without changing amount or spending.
Foreign-player callbacks cannot consume the owner response; duplicate, stale and post-cancel callbacks cannot mutate a newer page.
Cancel restores the most recently queued plus/minus amount; failed native send restores usable amount controls.
Unrelated inventory navigation and disconnect/reconnect invalidate pending amount responses; missing text safely restores controls.
A real sixty-second server timer restores the current amount, dismisses the dialog and rejects expired callbacks on both normal boots.
Existing queued plus/minus controls preserve exact native inventory and synthetic InventoryView references, cursor item and open/close counts.
Queued Save/Review uses latest amount; checkout, duplicate final confirmation, physical protection, restart, missing Economy and missing Vault regression checks pass.
limitations: Capturing showDialog and dispatching a synthetic response proves server construction/callback handling, not real Java rendering or protocol support.
Human mouse-pointer position, client packets, Bedrock rendering, phone keyboard/layout and actual Geyser/Floodgate were not tested.
Actual installed economy and GriefPrevention versions, real player save persistence and other-plugin interference were not tested.
Legacy migration tests remain supported but were not rerun for this UI-only candidate; historical migration evidence does not constitute a fresh run.
Runtime fixture logs include external Paper-update and Minecraft authentication DNS warnings; no live accounts or network clients were used.
